summary: T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later serving there (~1953–1967), at Oxford (~1949–1950), and at McMaster University (~1970–1972).
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held posts at the University of Madras, where he is attested in 1994 and as a professor in 2008.

T. S. Eliot (1888–1965) studied at Milton Academy, Harvard, the University of Paris, and Merton College, under teachers including George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held posts at Birkbeck (~1916–1919) and the University of Chicago (~1950).

T. S. Rukmani (b. 1932) is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held posts at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and Concordia University, where she was Chairperson of Hindu Studies in 1989.

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested between 1972 and 2007, serving there as professor from around 1984 to 1992.
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested as a Pandit in 1993 and as a professor in 2026.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he was attested as an Editorial Committee member in 2001 and as Deputy Director in 2026.

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (b. 1933) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Mysore, later holding posts at Kanakapura (1955), St. Joseph's (1957–1959), Osmania (1959–1968), Mysore (1968, 1984–1994), and Kannada University (1997).
T. Venkatacharya is an Indologist who held posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (attested 1971) and served as a professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and held professorships at the University of London (1882–1904) and Manchester (1904–1915).
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa (b. 1937), a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Kyoto University. He held posts at Tokai University, Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism, and Toho Gakkai.

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and archaeology. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (1988–2006), Nara University, Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1892 to 1895 and later served there as professor emeritus (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani (b. 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, and served as professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Milewski (1906–1966) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Lviv (1925–1929) and completed his habilitation at Jagiellonian University. He was Professor of General Linguistics at Lublin (1945–1950) and Jagiellonian University (1949–1966).
Tadeusz Pobożniak (1910–1991) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. (~1931–1938) and Ph.D. (by 1948) at Jagiellonian University, where he later served as professor (~1971–1975).

Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He received his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978 and later served there at SOAS as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).
